metadata.note: The Air Line, New Haven - Middletown - Willimantic, Connecticut (54.1 mi), and its 3.6-mile Colchester branch. Opened by the New Haven, Middletown and Willimantic Railroad to Middletown on 1 Aug 1870 and through to Willimantic in Aug 1873; reorganised after foreclosure as the Boston and New York Air-Line in 1875; leased to the New York, New Haven and Hartford from 1 Oct 1882 as its "Air Line Division". Passenger trains ended in late Jan 1928, replaced by New England Transportation Co. buses. In the 1880s-1890s it carried the Boston - New York through expresses (New England Limited, the White "Ghost" Train, the Air Line Limited) west of Willimantic; those are not drawn separately (report block [8]) - they ran on this geometry, in NH colour from 1882. Research report: research/branches/air_line_railroad.txt.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_and_New_York_Air-Line_Railroad -- en.wikipedia (cites Karr, The Rail Lines of Southern New England, 2nd ed. 2017, pp.82-88; NH local timetables 1912 and 1915)
https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/southernnewenglandrrs2.pdf -- John Fowler, Southern New England Railroads (2), line 141
https://www.loc.gov/resource/sn84022396/1939-08-31/ed-1/?sp=7 -- "Famous New Haven Trains - The Ghost Train", NH Along the Line Oct 1924, reprinted Putnam Patriot 1939

Colchester branch: B&NY Air Line 1877-1882 | NH 1882-1922 [OPEN], identical geometry. Report blocks [4] and [5] (NH, New Haven - Middletown and Middletown - Willimantic, same operator and years) are drawn as one feature; the report split them only to check the two halves separately. New colours: NHM&W #209010, B&NY Air Line #68C8C8 (no company in data/ used either); New Haven #7209B7 pulled from the existing NH features.
omitted: Report block [8], the through Boston - New York trains (New England Limited, White Train, Air Line Limited): not separate geometry; they ran on the features drawn here.

All freight-only years: the whole Air Line after Jan 1928 (Portland - Willimantic freight to 1965; New Haven - Portland still freight), and the Colchester branch after its unestablished passenger end.
Cedar Hill Yard employees' stop: not public passenger service.
metadata.existing_layer_note: No existing feature drew any part of Cedar Hill - Middletown - Willimantic or the Colchester branch. The New Haven Union Station - Cedar Hill track (~2-3 mi) is also drawn by nynhh-new-haven-springfield (hartford_and_new_haven_railroad.geojson); the NY&NE layer ends at Willimantic and correctly draws nothing west of it.
not_yet_sourced: nynhh-colchester-branch: [OPEN] end - passenger service confirmed only to Jan 1922; actual end (between 1922 and Jan 1928) not found (report U3).
bnyal-new-haven-willimantic / nynhh-air-line boundary: 1 Oct 1882 lease vs uncited claims of NH operation from 1879 (report U1).
bnyal-colchester-branch: operator between opening (3 Aug 1877) and the Air Line lease (3 Apr 1878) not established.
Exact 1875 reorganisation date (NHM&W -> B&NY Air Line); Willimantic opening day 16 vs 12 Aug 1873; New England Limited start 10 vs 18 Nov 1884 (report U5).
Middletown terminal arrangements 1870-1875 and the date Air Line trains began using the later union station (report U4).
All headways and speeds: no legible Air Line timetable was read for any year (report U7).
Later history of the 1873 Connecticut River swing bridge (rebuild date) not researched.

segments.note: First section of the Air Line, opened New Haven - Middletown on Monday 1 Aug 1870 (ALT24, the NH's own 1924 history; en.wikipedia/Karr pp.82-88 agree on 1870). Ends in Aug 1873 only as an era: the line was extended through to Willimantic and continues as feature nhmw-new-haven-willimantic. The Boston, Hartford and Erie took a lease in 1873 that was forfeited before the extension opened - it never ran these trains. Fowler's 1876 Pathfinder letter (y) at Montowese, Northford and Rockfall confirms the stations. The 1870s Middletown terminal was not the later union station the geometry ends at (see geometry_quality). Headway is an estimate (about 3-4 trains each way a day); no NHM&W-era timetable was read.

segments.note: The reorganised Boston and New York Air-Line Railroad (1875, exact date not found; en.wikipedia, Rapallo Viaduct article and a trail-kiosk blog agree on the year). From Mon 12 Jun 1876 the New York and New England ran through cars Boston - New York "by the New Air Line road via Middletown and Willimantic" (Boston Advertiser ad quoted in ALT24); who supplied motive power west of Willimantic 1876-1882 was not established. Fowler's 1876 Pathfinder letter (y) is present at every station from Montowese to Turnerville. Ends 30 Sep 1882: the New York, New Haven and Hartford took it on a 99-year lease from 1 Oct 1882 (1905 directory via search summary only; Blackledge River Railroad Bridge article; ALT24 "consolidated ... and became the Air Line Division" 30 Sep 1882). SOURCE CONFLICT: the Rapallo Viaduct article and the PedalPoint blog say the NH leased it in 1879, and the Air Line State Park Trail article says "operated by the New Haven from 1879" - all uncited; if that is right the colour boundary moves to 1879, the drawn passenger years do not. Headway is an estimate (about 3-4 trains each way a day plus the through cars).

segments.note: The NH's "Air Line Division" from its lease of 1 Oct 1882. Through Boston - New York expresses used it with NH engines west of Willimantic: the New England Limited from Nov 1884 (10 Nov per ALT24 reprints vs 18 Nov per this repo's NY&NE research - conflict recorded), the White ("Ghost") Train 16 Mar 1891 - 20 Oct 1895 and the Air Line Limited from Oct 1895, which "ran until 1902" (UConn Archives blog); an uncited claim that through trains lasted to 1924 (abandonedrails.com) was not verified. Positive dated evidence of local service: NH timetable ad 14 May 1903 for the "Air Line Division" with connections at Middletown and at Turnerville for the Colchester branch (JC03); Fowler letters z (1893/96), a (1904) and b (1920) at every station. The 1912-1913 burial of the Lyman and Rapallo viaducts kept the same alignment. This segment ends at Jan 1922 only to mark the cut in service (next segment). Headway is an ESTIMATE: about 4-6 trains each way a day 1903-1920 (JC03 lists several departures but its times are OCR-mangled) - not a sourced frequency.

segments.note: Reduced service. A new NH timetable from 22 Jan 1922 took off two Willimantic - New Haven Air Line trains, leaving others running (Norwich Bulletin 28 Jan 1922); passenger train No. 22 over the Air Line Division derailed at Willimantic in Aug 1922; an East Hampton - Middletown school train ran in Dec 1925 (New Britain Herald 14 Dec 1925); from 26 Sep 1927 two Air Line trains left Willimantic on weekdays, "one being a mixed train to New Haven and the other run to Middletown" (Windham County Observer 28 Sep 1927). Passenger service ended about Sat 28 Jan 1928, when conductor Marshall Porter "concludes service on that branch today" (New Britain Herald 28 Jan 1928); New England Transportation Co. buses New Haven - Willimantic from Sun 29 Jan 1928 "take the place of the passenger train service on the Air Line Division ... which has been discontinued" (Weekly Gazette 27 Jan and 3 Feb 1928). The uncited "by 1937" end in the Rapallo Viaduct article and elsewhere is contradicted by these and appears to belong to the NY&NE side (report U2). Freight continued: New Haven - Middletown - Portland is still freight track, and Portland - Willimantic was abandoned in 1965 (en.wikipedia) - context only, not drawn. Headway is an ESTIMATE from the two daily departures counted in 1922 and 1927.
sources: Segment-level: research report research/branches/air_line_railroad.txt blocks [4]-[5] - NB22c (Jan 1922), NB22e (Aug 1922), NBH25 (Dec 1925), WCO27 (Sep 1927), NBH28, WG28a, WG28b (Jan 1928 end). Headway estimated from NB22c and WCO27 departure counts.

Junction taken where the Colchester Spur trail leaves the Air Line State Park Trail west of Amston; the branch then follows the "Air Line State Park Trail - Colchester Spur" (OSM cycleway, the lifted grade) and its named service-road continuation to the Colchester depot site. No other approximation; no later-alignment issue known.

segments.note: Turnerville (later Amston) - Colchester, 3.6 mi, no intermediate stations. Built by the Colchester Railway Company, whose sole stockholder was the town of Colchester (Norwich Bulletin 17 Jan 1922); opened 3 Aug 1877 and leased to the Boston and New York Air Line on 3 Apr 1878 for 999 years (Blackledge River Railroad Bridge article). WHO RAN THE TRAINS between opening and the Apr 1878 lease is NOT ESTABLISHED; it is drawn in Air Line colour from opening because the Air Line was the lessee within eight months and nothing shows the Colchester Railway running trains itself. Passengers in 1877 are not in doubt, only the operator. Ends 30 Sep 1882 as an era: leased with the Air Line to the NH from 1 Oct 1882 (feature nynhh-colchester-branch). Headway is an estimate.

OpenHistoricalMap way -199476944 (Willimantic - Cedar Hill, 50 mi) also served as an independent check of the whole trace.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 3.51 mi against 3.6 mi documented (en.wikipedia station table; Blackledge River Railroad Bridge article 3.59 mi; Fowler Amston MP 44.2 to Colchester 47.8). Junction taken where the Colchester Spur trail leaves the Air Line State Park Trail west of Amston; the branch then follows the "Air Line State Park Trail - Colchester Spur" (OSM cycleway, the lifted grade) and its named service-road continuation to the Colchester depot site. One 204 m straight link joins the trail end to the service road. The c.0.1-0.2 mi shortfall against 3.6 mi is probably the difference between the trail junction and Amston station, where the mileage was counted. No other approximation; no later-alignment issue known.

segments.note: NH branch service from the 1 Oct 1882 lease (the NH bought the town of Colchester's interest in the Colchester Railway in 1905 - a stock purchase, not an operator change). Positive evidence: NH timetable ad 14 May 1903, "at Turnerville with Colchester branch" (JC03); Fowler letters z (1893/96), a (1904), b (1920) at Colchester; in 1917 the branch carried "nearly a thousand summer boarders" (Norwich Bulletin 9 Jun 1917); in Jan 1922 the NH announced it would "discontinue all passenger service on the Colchester branch" and the next day withdrew the plan - "the same schedule will be maintained as before" (Norwich Bulletin 17 and 18 Jan 1922). [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed only to Jan 1922. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when branch passenger service actually stopped (the Air Line's own trains ended Jan 1928, which bounds it only by inference; by 1951 the Official Guide marks Colchester freight-only). Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate.

End year is the last confirmed year [OPEN]. Headway not sourced.
